guarantees.claim: tx_enable equals reg2hw.ctrl.tx.q, rx_enable equals reg2hw.ctrl.rx.q, rxnf_enable equals reg2hw.ctrl.nf.q, sys_loopback equals reg2hw.ctrl.slpbk.q, line_loopback equals reg2hw.ctrl.llpbk.q—all driven continuously from the register-to-HW bus.
uart_fifo_rxrst equals reg2hw.fifo_ctrl.rxrst.q AND reg2hw.fifo_ctrl.rxrst.qe (hardware qualifier).
uart_fifo_rxilvl equals reg2hw.fifo_ctrl.rxilvl.q and uart_fifo_txilvl equals reg2hw.fifo_ctrl.txilvl.q, continuously.
ovrd_tx_en equals reg2hw.ovrd.txen.q and ovrd_tx_val equals reg2hw.ovrd.txval.q, unconditionally.

assumptions.claim: For the FIFO reset signals to become active, the corresponding qualifier enable bits (reg2hw.fifo_ctrl.rxrst.qe / txrst.qe) must be asserted together with the reset request bits (rxrst.q / txrst.q). The external logic writing to the register must ensure this two‑bit protocol is followed.
assumptions.cond: when a RX or TX FIFO reset is intended
assumptions.risk: If the qualifier bits are not set while the request bits are set, uart_fifo_rxrst / uart_fifo_txrst remain low, leaving the FIFOs in a non-reset state despite a software‑initiated reset write.

uncertain_points.claim: The signals ovrd_tx_en and ovrd_tx_val are driven directly from the reg2hw override fields, potentially allowing an external override of the TX data path for test or debug. The security impact of setting these overrides is not clear from this chunk alone.
uncertain_points.cond: when ovrd_tx_en is asserted, ovrd_tx_val is injected
uncertain_points.risk: An unintended or malicious assertion of ovrd_tx_en could bypass the normal transmit FIFO and control logic, possibly leading to unexpected transmission, protocol violations, or leakage of internal test values.
